options: Deletes rows from the majority class until the classes match
Weights each class inversely to its frequency so rare-class errors count more
Forces the model to predict both classes equally often
Duplicates the minority rows in the dataset
questions.explain: Balanced weighting scales each class by n_samples / (n_classes * class_count). The data is unchanged; the loss simply counts rare-class mistakes more heavily.

questions.q: In the lesson's example the plain model had 97% accuracy but the highest cost. Why?
options: Accuracy cannot be computed for imbalanced data
It made too many false alarms
It missed most true positives, and misses were 20 times more expensive than false alarms
It was trained on the test set
questions.explain: The plain model caught only 44% of positives. With a miss costing 100 and a false alarm 5, those misses dominated the total cost even though accuracy looked excellent.

questions.q: A stakeholder says a missed case is twice as costly as a false alarm. What is a sensible way to use that?
options: Ignore it; costs never affect model choice
Use it to set a class weight ratio or threshold and choose on validation data
Delete all false alarms from the test set
Tune the weight on the test set until recall is highest
questions.explain: Business costs are exactly what guide weights and thresholds. Select them on validation data, keeping the test set untouched for the final estimate.

questions.q: In scikit-learn 1.1, HistGradientBoostingClassifier has no class_weight argument. What can you do?
options: Pass sample_weight to fit, built with compute_sample_weight
Nothing; weighting is impossible for boosting
Set n_estimators to the class ratio
Switch to accuracy as the metric
questions.explain: Most estimators accept sample_weight in fit. compute_sample_weight("balanced", y) produces per-row weights that behave like class weights.

questions.q: Inside a Pipeline whose final step is named "model", how do you pass sample weights to it?
options: pipe.fit(X, y, sample_weight=w) always works for every step
pipe.fit(X, y, weights=w)
pipe.fit(X, y, model__sample_weight=w)
It cannot be done inside a pipeline
questions.explain: Pipeline routes fit parameters using the step name, two underscores, and the parameter name: model__sample_weight.
